messages.subject: Cut Point use in GGIR
parts:
Hello,

I hope this email finds you well. 
 I have some questions on the use of cut-point for GGIR MVPA, Light PA, MOD, and Vigorous thresholds. I plan to use the Chandler children vector magnitude (VM) cut-point which are < 305 (sedentary), 306 - 817 (Light physical activity), 818 - 1968 (Moderate PA), and >1969 (Vigorous PA). My question is:

1. Do I need to convert the vector magnitude (VM) cut-point to mg before inserting the values or I can use the VM cut-point directly in GGIR without conversion? 
Because when I tried using the VM directly on GGIR there was barely any output on moderate and vigorous intensity. Since these are raw children's accelerometry data, I expect values on moderate and vigorous PA. 

Thank you for your help.

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Cut Point use in GGIR
parts:
Hi John,

You need to make sure GGIR extracts the acceleration metric that matches the acceleration metric used for the cut-points.

By default GGIR only calculates ENMO in mg, so I any cut-point provided is assumed to be an ENMO cut-point.

You did not provide a reference for Chandler cutpoints but if Chanler cut-points were express in ActiGraphy counts then see:
https://wadpac.github.io/GGIR/articles/CutPoints.html#cut-points-not-expressed-in-gravitational-units-not-in-this-vignette
https://wadpac.github.io/GGIR/articles/GGIRParameters.html#do-neishabouricounts

Note that cut-points are specified differently for GGIR part 2 and 5:
https://wadpac.github.io/GGIR/articles/chapter11_DescribingDataCutPoints.html

Best wishes,

Vincent

Dr. Vincent van Hees | Independent consultant | https://accelting.com/
